summary: Design an ML-enhanced receiver chain for IoT-to-LEO-satellite communication, where conventional signal-processing algorithms (e.g., channel estimation, synchronization, detection) are augmented or replaced by learned models under low-SNR, high-Doppler, and resource-constrained IoT conditions.
assumptions: The IoT devices use narrowband waveforms (e.g., NB-IoT over satellite or LoRa-like modulation) with extreme Doppler shifts due to LEO satellite motion.
The receiver runs on the satellite or a ground station with moderate compute, permitting offline-trained deep models but limited on-device retraining.
Conventional model-based receivers (matched filter, pilot-based channel estimation, Viterbi decoding) are available as baselines; ML components are inserted piecewise at bottleneck stages.
Training data consists of simulated channel realizations covering diverse orbit geometries, weather conditions, and interference patterns, supplemented by a limited set of over-the-air recordings.
